full_judgment:
Mahmud Husain, J: This petition for special leave to appeal by the judgment-debtor is against the decision of a Division Bench of the High Court Division dismissing Appeal from Original Order No.67 of 1971 arising out of the judgment and order of the Subordinate Judge, 1st Court, Dacca in Miscellaneous Case No.185 of 1970. Respondent decree-holder obtained a compromise decree against the petitioner and under the terms of the compromise, the decretal amount of Rs. 66,056.5-6/ pies was payable by the petitioner in annual installment amounting Rs. 8,000/-. The petitioner made payment of two installments amounting Rs. 16,000/- and thereafter defaulted So, the respondent put the decree into execution being the Money Execution, Case No.1 of 1960 in which the respondent certified receipt of payment of Rs. 16,000/- and prayed for recovery of the balance. The petitioner thereafter paid Rs. 10,000/- out of Court. The said Money Execution Case No.1 of 1960 was dismissed for non-prosecution on 15.12.67 

 On 1.5.1968 the respondent started a fresh execution case being Money Execution Case No. 12 of 1968. In the application for execution of the decree the column Nos. 5,6 and 7 have not been filled in correctly. (In column No. 5 “Payment or adjustment made, if any with date”). Only Rs. 10,000/- was shown to have been paid. In column No.6 (Previous application, if any, with date and result) “M/Ex.1/60 dated 16.12.67” was noted. In column No.7 (Amount with interest, if any, due upon the decree or other etc.) was filled in as follows:- 

 The petitioner filed an objection under section 47 of the Code of Civil Procedure which was registered as Miscellaneous Case No. 185 of 1970 and stated that the Money Execution Case No. 12 of 1968 was time barred and not maintainable and that the columns in the application for execution of the decree had not been correctly filled in and as such it was not in accordance with law and that notice of execution was not served on the petitioner. The respondent opposed the said Miscellaneous Case by filing written objection and denied the allegations made therein. The learned Subordinate Judge dismissed the Miscellaneous Case with a direction to substitute the figure in column No. 5 of the application for execution by the figure “Rs. 16,000/- and to take early steps to add the result of the previous execution case in column No.6 

 “ I. Because the decree-holder did not disclose certified payments of Taka 16, 000/- in Column 5 of the application for execution and showed and exaggerated amount of principal as well as amount of interest contrary to the terms of the decree in Column 7 thereof, the application was not in accordance with the law at the time when it was presented and in view of the provisions of section 48 of the Code of Civil Procedure, the Executing Court had no jurisdiction to allow amendments thereto so as to transform it into a fresh application after expiry of the period of limitation.” 

 These substituted words cast a duty upon the court to see that the defect, if any, in the application for execution of a decree is remedied.
